MEMORANDUM
TO: Physical-Environmental Resources Coordinating Commission
FROM: Bernard T. Carter, Assistant Commissioner
TITLE: Comments concerning the Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972.
DATE: April 12, 1972
I have reviewed the Draft Environmental Statement proposed for the Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972 prepared by the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife. On Page 6, third line from the bottom of the page, the word authorized should be deleted and the word directed substituted in the Act. A proposed new sentence would be, "The Secretary would be directed wherever and whenever possible to enter into agreements with the states --".
I seriously question the exemption of American Indians, Aleuts and Eskimos from the prohibition in taking and importing endangered species. If the species are truly endangered, then it should be protected totally.
On Pages 7 and 8 my comment would be that the jurisdiction by the Secretary of Commerce for some species should be climinated from the legislation. The Department of Interior should have sole jurisdiction of the endangered species.
I endorse Alternate 1 in the Draft Statement.
On Page 8 I would question, who determines whether a Federal agencies' policies or programs jeopardize the "continued existence of an endangered species?" Some of the Department of Adriculture's programs, such as channelization, spraying of pesticides and land clearing certainly are decreasing habitat for all species or directly affect them. It seems that an outside Review Board should be established to determine what programs are justifiable. If each department or agency was responsible for policing their own programs, I doubt if enforcement would be effective.
